stem:
Tara's calculator starts at $0$ and has buttons $+1$, $+10$, $+100$, and $+1000$. She wants the display to show exactly $240$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call the answer place-value buttons only, without saying which presses make $240$.
Say that reaching $240$ is what creates the $+10$ and $+100$ buttons.
Press $+100$ twice and $+10$ four times (or any regrouping that totals $240$), because many click mixes of powers of ten can make the same number.
Treat each button as multiplying the display by $10$, as if that were the same as adding powers of ten.

teacher.key_rationale: With powers-of-ten add buttons, many press mixes can make $240$ because $10$ of a smaller place equals $1$ of the next. Naming buttons alone, reversing goal and buttons, or swapping addition for multiply-by-$10$ all leave that test.
